title: Reliable API Clients: Timeouts, Status Codes and Retry Policy
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and behaviour of Reliable API Clients: Timeouts, Status Codes and Retry Policy.
Choose an appropriate reliable api clients: timeouts, status codes and retry policy technique for an application.
Interpret representative code and output involving reliable api clients: timeouts, status codes and retry policy.
Identify limitations and failure modes for reliable api clients: timeouts, status codes and retry policy.
Apply the concepts in maintainable Python code.

understand.concept: A reliable API client distinguishes transport failures, HTTP status errors and invalid response data. Timeouts bound waiting, status codes describe the server's response, and retries can recover from transient failures. Retrying is not always safe: non-idempotent operations such as creating a payment may be duplicated unless the API provides an idempotency mechanism. Backoff and retry limits protect both client and service.
understand.whyItMatters: Reliability controls make integrations predictable during network failures and service overload.
understand.analogy: A delivery service may retry a missed connection, but it should not place the same paid order twice.
understand.analogyLimit: A retry policy cannot fix permanent errors or guarantee that a timed-out operation did not already succeed on the server.
understand.summary: Reliable API Clients: Timeouts, Status Codes and Retry Policy develops practical application engineering skills for Python projects.

explain.narrative:
## Make failure behaviour explicit
Classify errors before deciding what to do. A 4xx response often indicates a request or permission problem; 5xx responses may be transient, but the API contract decides. Retry only operations safe to repeat, use a finite attempt count and exponential backoff with jitter in production. Honour Retry-After where supported. Log a request identifier and status, but never credentials or sensitive payloads. Validate decoded response content independently.
